01. What is your highest level of education completed? Options: High School or Equivalent | Some College | Bachelor's Degree | Master's Degree or higher

02. How many years of experience do have in administrative leadership in higher education, including significant responsibility for institutional or organizational leadership? Options: Less than 1 year | 1 -2 years | 3 - 4 years | 5 or more. years
Possession of a master's degree from an accredited college or university.
A minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible administrative leadership experience in higher education, including significant responsibility for institutional or organizational leadership.
Provide visionary and strategic leadership for the College and advance its mission, goals, and priorities in alignment with the strategic direction of the Peralta Community College District.
Lead institutional planning and transformation efforts that strengthen student success, educational excellence, equity, enrollment, and the overall effectiveness of the College.
Oversee the College’s academic, student services, administrative, and operational functions and ensure effective coordination of programs and services.
Develop and maintain a sustainable fiscal framework for the College, including budget development, resource allocation, and responsible stewardship of College and District resources.
Lead efforts to recruit, retain, and support students and strengthen enrollment, persistence, completion, transfer, and workforce outcomes.
Foster a culture of equity, inclusion, collaboration, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement among faculty, staff, administrators, and students.
Promote effective shared governance and maintain productive relationships with faculty, staff, collective bargaining representatives, student leaders, and other College constituencies.
Recruit, develop, and evaluate members of the College’s leadership team and establish organizational structures that support effective performance and accountability.
Ensure compliance with Board policies, District procedures, collective bargaining agreements, accreditation standards, and applicable laws and regulations.

Build and maintain strong relationships with community, educational, governmental, workforce, philanthropic, and other external partners to advance the College’s mission and expand opportunities and resources for students.
Serve as the College’s principal representative to the community and, as appropriate, represent the College within the District, region, state, and higher education community.

Collaborate with the Chancellor, other College Presidents, and District leadership on District-wide initiatives, policies, and priorities while advancing the distinctive mission and needs of the College.
Keep the Chancellor and Board of Trustees informed of the College’s performance, priorities, challenges, and opportunities and provide recommendations regarding matters affecting the College.
Perform other duties as assigned.
The mission, organization, governance, and role of California community colleges.
Articulate and advance a compelling vision for the College while aligning College priorities with District goals.
Higher education administration, including academic affairs, student services, enrollment management, institutional effectiveness, and administrative operations.
Lead effectively in a complex, diverse, and highly collaborative environment.
Current issues, trends, and challenges affecting community colleges and the diverse communities they serve.
Inspire, develop, and hold accountable a high-performing leadership team.
Strategic planning, organizational development, fiscal management, and resource allocation.
Make difficult decisions thoughtfully and transparently while maintaining trust and productive relationships.
Student success, equity, access, enrollment, retention, and completion strategies.
Balance competing priorities and allocate resources strategically in support of institutional goals.
Shared governance, collective bargaining, and collaborative decision-making in a higher education environment.
Work effectively with faculty, staff, students, administrators, collective bargaining representatives, the Chancellor, Board of Trustees, and community partners.
Applicable federal and California laws, regulations, and policies governing community colleges.
Represent the College and District with credibility, integrity, cultural competence, and professionalism.
Providing visionary, strategic, and student-centered leadership.
Navigate complex organizational, political, and community environments while maintaining focus on the College’s mission and students.
Leading organizational change and institutional transformation.
Developing collaborative relationships and building trust among diverse constituencies.
Strategic and fiscal planning and resource management.
Analyzing complex institutional issues and using data to inform decisions.
Conflict resolution, negotiation, consensus building, and problem-solving.
Communicating effectively with a wide range of internal and external audiences.
Building effective partnerships with educational institutions, employers, community organizations, government agencies, and other stakeholders.
Understanding of, sensitivity to and respect for the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, disabilityand ethnic backgrounds of Peralta Colleges’ students, faculty, staff and community.
Foster a culture of student success, equity, innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Accreditation, institutional effectiveness, assessment, and accountability.
Lead through significant change while maintaining institutional stability, employee engagement, and organizational effectiveness.
